subject.title: feat(tui): add /upload command for file context

question: Should the core TUI own and reserve a built-in `/upload` command that reads local files into the next chat turn, or should this be routed through an existing Gateway/plugin/file-context boundary first?
rationale: The workflow is useful, but choosing the permanent command namespace and file-ingestion owner affects dynamic plugin commands and security boundaries; automation should not make that product/API decision.

options.title: Confirm Core TUI Upload
options.body: Reserve `/upload` for core TUI, then require the rebase and safety/lifecycle repairs before merge.

options.title: Use Existing File Boundaries
options.body: Pause this branch and ask for a narrower design that reuses Gateway input-file handling or another existing attachment boundary.

options.title: Defer The Feature
options.body: Close or leave dormant until a maintainer sponsors local file-context UX across CLI, TUI, and Gateway consistently.

recommendation.title: Confirm Core TUI Upload
recommendation.body: Reserve `/upload` for core TUI, then require the rebase and safety/lifecycle repairs before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and merged PRs make steipete the clearest owner for TUI command/session lifecycle and the security boundary touched here.
